_comment: Annotated screenshots for the guides (docs/*.md, read in the app under Clientst0r Docs).
Each entry's annotate list draws numbered callouts; its note is the legend the guide prints
under the image, in the same order. Capture against the isolated demo instance with:
Selectors are Playwright selectors, so :has-text() and :text-is() work.

screenshots.name: guide-dashboard
screenshots.alt: The dashboard with numbered callouts on the sidebar, Go to, the client switcher, the ticket queue, Customize and the Clientst0r Docs link

annotate.note: The sidebar: nine work sections. Only the current one is open; type in Jump to to filter every page you may open.
Go to (Ctrl+K): open any page, setting or record by name.
The client switcher: the customer you are working for. Pages show that customer's records. Superusers can also choose Global View.
Your ticket queue, with SLA due times.
Customize: choose and arrange the dashboard panels.
Clientst0r Docs: these guides, searchable, in the app.

screenshots.caption: The dashboard, sidebar and top bar.

screenshots.name: guide-docs-viewer
screenshots.alt: Clientst0r Docs: the search box, guide categories, a screenshot count badge and the sidebar link

annotate.note: Search every guide. Results list the matching sections with your words highlighted, and open the guide at that section.
Guides by subject.
The number of screenshots in a guide.
Open the docs from any page, at the foot of the sidebar (also linked in the page footer).

screenshots.caption: Clientst0r Docs in the app.

screenshots.name: guide-ticket
screenshots.alt: A ticket with numbered callouts on the next step, the conversation, the reply composer and the devices panel

annotate.note: Next step: what the ticket is waiting for (here, a reply to the customer).
The conversation: the request, replies, internal notes (marked STAFF ONLY) and status changes, oldest first.
Reply or add an internal note. Pick a canned response, attach files, copy people in (Cc).
Devices on this ticket, with RMM tools when an RMM is paired.

screenshots.caption: Working a ticket.

screenshots.name: guide-client-overview
screenshots.alt: A customer's workspace with numbered callouts on the customer bar, quick actions, key figures, open tickets and open invoices

annotate.note: The customer you are viewing, with links back to all clients and to Global View.
Quick actions for this customer: ticket, contact, asset, project, document, quote.
Key figures: open tickets, SLA at risk, managed assets and more.
Open tickets, with SLA breaches and those at risk.
Open invoices and the balance owed.

screenshots.caption: A customer's workspace (Clients → the customer).

screenshots.name: guide-billing-ready
screenshots.alt: Agreement billing review with numbered callouts on the month, tickets for billing, a customer's ready lines, Approve and the consolidated draft button

annotate.note: The billing month. Step back or forward a month.
Tickets for billing: tickets whose time and items are waiting to be billed.
Ready for billing, per customer: the exact lines an invoice would carry, with amounts ready and on hold.
Approve, hold or exclude lines before invoicing.

annotate.selector: button:has-text("Create one consolidated draft for selected")
annotate.note: Create draft invoices: one per ticket, or one consolidated draft per customer.

screenshots.caption: Business → Billing → Billing Review.

screenshots.name: guide-system-updates
screenshots.alt: System Updates with numbered callouts on the installed version, the update channel, the update status, available versions and backups

annotate.note: The version installed, and the release it came from.
Update channel: Official release (recommended) or Preview / testing.
Whether a newer release is available. Check now asks GitHub straight away; Apply installs it.
Available versions, each with its release notes.
The backup taken before every update, and rollback.

screenshots.caption: Administration → System → System Updates.

screenshots.name: guide-offhost-backups
screenshots.alt: Off-host Backups with numbered callouts on the status, Back up now, the encryption key, the destination and the schedule

annotate.note: Status: last backup, last verification, and anything that needs attention.
Back up now, or verify the newest archive now.
Step 1, the backup key. Store it somewhere that is not this server before you rely on backups.
Step 2, where archives go: an SFTP server (approve its host key) or a mounted directory.
Step 3, how often to back up and verify, and how many archives to keep.

screenshots.caption: Administration → Maintenance → Off-host Backups.

screenshots.name: guide-roles
screenshots.alt: Roles with numbered callouts on the built-in roles, Create custom role, Compare, Why does someone have access, and Access groups

annotate.note: Built-in roles. Assign one to a person, or copy it as the start of a custom role.
Create a custom role with exactly the permissions you choose.
Compare roles side by side.
Why does someone have access? Pick a person and a permission to see which role grants it.
Access groups: limit which customers a group of technicians can see.

screenshots.caption: Administration → Users & Access → Roles.

screenshots.name: guide-connected-apps
screenshots.alt: Connected Applications with numbered callouts on the connections list, Connect, Create invitation code and the emergency kill switch

annotate.note: Connections: the applications paired with this installation, and their health.
Connect an application: start pairing from this side.
Or create an invitation code for the other application to use.
Emergency kill switch: stop every connection at once.

screenshots.caption: Administration → Integrations → Connected Applications.

screenshots.name: guide-my-queue
screenshots.alt: My Work → My Queue with numbered callouts on the My Work tabs, the Mine / All customers switch, running timers, tickets near SLA breach, my open tickets and unacknowledged alerts

annotate.note: The My Work tabs: your queue, tasks, timesheet, schedule, leave and more. You see only the tabs your role allows.
Mine shows the customers you work for; All customers widens the waiting queues, devices and alerts to every customer you can reach.
Timers you left running, with Stop.
Tickets due within two hours or already breached. Work it opens the ticket.
Your open tickets, soonest SLA first. View all opens the same list in Tickets.
Unacknowledged RMM and security alerts at your customers, each with Review or Open device.

screenshots.caption: My Work → My Queue.

screenshots.name: guide-timesheet-approvals
screenshots.alt: Timesheet Approvals with numbered callouts on the filters, bulk approve and reject, a pending week, the payroll CSV link and recent decisions

annotate.note: Filter by technician, and the recent decisions by approved or rejected.
Tick weeks, add an optional note, then Approve selected or Reject selected.
A submitted week: the technician, the week, entry and minute totals and their comment. Open it to send single entries back.
Payroll CSV: approved weeks for the last 30 days, one row per technician and week.
The last 50 decisions, with who decided and their notes.

screenshots.caption: My Work → Timesheet Approvals.

screenshots.name: guide-my-leave
screenshots.alt: My Leave with numbered callouts on Request Leave, the pending requests with Cancel, upcoming approved leave and past requests

annotate.note: Request Leave: type, dates, half day and a note for the approver.
Requests waiting for a decision. Cancel withdraws one.
Approved leave that has not ended yet.
Everything else: past, denied and cancelled requests.

screenshots.caption: My Work → My Leave.

screenshots.name: guide-my-resources
screenshots.alt: My Resources with numbered callouts on skills, certifications, leave this year, billable target and working hours

annotate.note: Your skills, with proficiency and years of experience.
Certifications with issuer and expiry. SOON marks one that expires within 60 days.
This year's leave: approved and pending requests and days used.
Your weekly billable-hours target, and your loaded cost rate (MSP staff only).
The days and hours you work. Dispatch and routing use them when you have no shift.

screenshots.caption: My Work → My Resources.

screenshots.name: guide-shift-schedule
screenshots.alt: Shift Schedule with numbered callouts on the week navigation, the team filter, the week grid and pending leave, and the form for adding a weekly shift

annotate.note: Shifts & Locations: Shift Schedule, Location Sharing and Timeclock. Configure holds shift templates and dispatch location settings.
Step a week back or forward, or return to this week.
People who can see the team choose all technicians or one team.
One row per technician: shifts, approved and pending leave, and holidays. A shift that clashes with leave is marked in red.
Shift managers add a shift template to a technician or team on chosen weekdays. Until a template exists, it asks you to create one first.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Shifts & Locations → Shift Schedule.

screenshots.name: guide-scheduled-tasks
screenshots.alt: Scheduled Tasks with numbered callouts on the Scheduling tabs, New Task, the filters, an overdue task and a recurring task

annotate.note: Scheduling: All Tasks, My Tasks and Calendar.
New Task: title, priority, due date, recurrence, who signs off and when to warn.
Filter by status and priority, or jump to your tasks or overdue ones.
An overdue task: past its due date and not yet completed.
A recurring task. When it is completed, the next occurrence is created.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Scheduling → All Tasks.

screenshots.name: guide-ticket-list
screenshots.alt: The ticket list with numbered callouts on the view tabs, the filter bar, a ticket subject, the Next column and the New ticket button

annotate.note: Views of the same list: All Tickets, Overview, My Queue, Unassigned, SLA, Escalated, and under More, Approvals (and AI Inbox when AI is on).
Filters: search, client, status, priority, category, queue, assignee, request type, age, SLA and sort. They are in the address, so a filtered list can be bookmarked.
The subject opens the ticket; the ticket number sits under it.
Next: whose move it is. Reply when the customer spoke last, waiting when you did.
New ticket.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Tickets → All Tickets.

screenshots.name: guide-ticket-unassigned
screenshots.alt: The Unassigned view with numbered callouts on the SLA column, the assignment picker and the Dispatch Board link

annotate.note: SLA state and time left (or overdue by). The list reads soonest deadline first.
Assign the ticket from the list. Shown only where you may assign it.
Open the Dispatch Board to plan the week instead.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Tickets → Unassigned.

screenshots.name: guide-ticket-work
screenshots.alt: A ticket's header and side column with numbered callouts on the priority, status, queue and assignee badges, the SLA badge, Watch, Actions, the closeout checklist and the Details card

annotate.note: Priority, then status, queue and assignee.
SLA state: on track, warning, breached (response or resolution) or paused.
Watch: get emails about new activity.
Actions: assign to me or a technician, change status, close with a resolution.
Closeout checklist: steps marked required must be ticked before the ticket can close; sign-off.
Details: type, source, impact, urgency, contact, site and asset.

screenshots.caption: A ticket: header and side column.

screenshots.name: guide-ticket-time
screenshots.alt: The Time and Charges card on a ticket with numbered callouts on the totals, the running timer, the time entry form and the logged entries

annotate.note: Total and billable minutes on this ticket.
A running timer: add a note, then Stop & log.
Log time by hand, or Start timer: minutes, classification, work type, role and notes.
Logged entries, with classification and agreement.

screenshots.caption: Time & Charges on a ticket.

screenshots.name: guide-dispatch-board
screenshots.alt: The Dispatch Board with numbered callouts on the Unassigned queue link, the Overdue panel, the Unassigned row, a technician row, the Other column and an assignment picker

annotate.note: Open unassigned tickets for the selected client, in the ticket list.
Overdue: open tickets whose due date has passed.
Unassigned tickets, by due day.
One row per technician; the envelope means they are emailed on assignment.
Other: no due date, or due outside the 7 days shown.
Assign from the card, or drag the card to a technician's row. The bulb lists suggested technicians.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Dispatch Board.

screenshots.name: guide-project
screenshots.alt: A project with numbered callouts on the project facts, Ready to bill, Profitability, Budget, the task tools, a task's Ticket button and the project's tickets

annotate.note: Client, owner, dates, estimated hours, billable. Edit changes them.
Ready to bill: what is waiting, and Create draft invoice (nothing is sent).
Profitability: revenue, labour cost and margin. Only staff allowed to see profitability.
Budget: hours and amount used against the budget.
Timeline, and Apply template: copy a template's tasks onto the project.
→ Ticket: make a task a ticket so time can be logged on it. Set assignee and status per task.
Tickets in this project.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Projects → a project.

screenshots.name: guide-service-catalog
screenshots.alt: The service catalog with numbered callouts on the tile and list switch, a catalog tile, its Edit button, Portal request types and forms, and New Catalog Item

annotate.note: Show the catalog as tiles or as a table. The page remembers your choice.
A catalog item. Click it to open a new ticket already filled in from this item; the badges show its default priority, queue and type.
Edit the item (MSP staff only).
Portal request types and forms: what customers can request in the portal.
Add a catalog item.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Service Management → Service Catalog.

screenshots.name: guide-change-requests
screenshots.alt: The change request list with numbered callouts on the status and risk filters, a change's ticket number, its risk and status, and the CAB columns

annotate.note: Filter by where the change is: draft, pending CAB approval, approved, implementing, verified and so on.
Filter by risk: low, medium, high or emergency.
One change. The number opens its change record; the ticket itself is a normal ticket of type Change.
Required CAB: how many approvers the change needs. Votes: how many have voted so far.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Service Management → Change Requests.

screenshots.name: guide-change-request
screenshots.alt: A change record with numbered callouts on its risk and status, the plans, the schedule, the CAB approval table and the actions

annotate.note: The change's risk and where it stands.
Implementation plan, rollback plan and impact assessment.
The planned window and, once work starts, the actual start and end.
Each required approver and their vote. All must approve, and none reject, before work can begin. With no required approvers, one approval is enough.
The next step: submit to CAB, begin implementation, or record the outcome.

screenshots.caption: A change record (Change Requests → a change).

screenshots.name: guide-problem
screenshots.alt: A problem record with numbered callouts on the root-cause analysis, related tickets, investigation notes and the status pipeline

annotate.note: Symptoms, root cause, workaround and permanent fix.
The incidents that share this cause. Link another by its ticket number.
What was learned and when. Mark a note as a breakthrough to make it stand out.
Move the problem on. Known error needs a root cause and workaround; resolved needs a root cause and permanent fix.

screenshots.caption: A problem record (Problems → a problem).

screenshots.name: guide-runbooks
screenshots.alt: The runbook list with numbered callouts on the run-as-ticket note, the filters, a runbook and New Workflow

annotate.note: Running a runbook opens a ticket that carries its checklist.
Search by title or description, or filter by category.
A runbook: its category, number of stages, tags, and whether it belongs to this customer (Org) or to every customer (Global).
Write a new runbook for the selected customer.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Workflows → Runbooks.

screenshots.name: guide-runbook
screenshots.alt: A runbook with numbered callouts on Launch Workflow, Edit, the flowchart button and the stages

annotate.note: Launch Workflow: pick the customer and assignee; a ticket opens with this checklist.
Edit or delete the runbook (not offered on global runbooks).
Draw a flowchart of the stages as a diagram.
The stages, in order. A stage can link a document, password, secure note or asset and can require confirmation.

screenshots.caption: A runbook (Runbooks → a runbook).

screenshots.name: guide-support-workflows-manage
screenshots.alt: The support workflow list with numbered callouts on New workflow, a built-in workflow, its alert categories and actions, and Edit and Turn off

annotate.note: Write a workflow of your own.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=0
annotate.note: A workflow, marked built-in, customised or off.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=1
annotate.note: The alert categories it is offered for.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr:has-text('Service stopped') >> td >> nth=2
annotate.note: The Rem0te catalog action a workflow may offer; most offer manual steps only.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=3
annotate.note: Edit it, turn it off or on, or Reset a customised built-in.

screenshots.caption: Service Desk → Workflows → Support Workflows.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-onboarding
screenshots.alt: The customer onboarding page with numbered callouts on the In progress list, Onboard a customer, and the change form for an existing customer

annotate.note: Sessions still open. Resume one from where it was left; recently closed sessions are listed below.
Start a new customer. Only the first step is required to create the customer.
For a change to an existing customer, pick the customer...
...and the change: plan change, users or devices added or removed, a location, renewal, price increase or offboarding.

screenshots.caption: Clients → Onboard Customer.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-list
screenshots.alt: The asset list with numbered callouts on Add Asset, the search box, the filter row, the Views bar, an asset name and the view and edit buttons

annotate.note: Add an asset by hand.
Search name, serial, asset tag, hostname, manufacturer and model.
Filters: type, status, location, manufacturer, and for technicians RMM state and active alerts. Sort and page size sit at the end.
Views: Needs reorder, and for technicians RMM offline, RMM alerts, RMM data stale and No RMM device. Save your own filter sets here too.

annotate.selector: main #assetTable tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=0
annotate.note: The picture and name. The name opens the asset; badges flag reorder, age, firmware and warranty when those checks are on.
View or edit the asset.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → All Assets.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-detail
screenshots.alt: An asset page with numbered callouts on the Device workspace button, Generate Profile, Edit, the tabs and the relationships

annotate.note: Device workspace: the technician's working view of this device.
Generate Profile: write the asset's fields (and linked RMM data) into a document.
Edit the asset, including its picture.
Details, Custom Fields, Ports, RMM, Serial history and Images. Ports and RMM appear only when there is something to show.
Relationships this asset starts, by kind (Depends On, Related and so on).

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → All Assets → an asset.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-serials
screenshots.alt: Serial History search results with numbered callouts on the search box, a serial with its latest event, the asset it belongs to and its event table

annotate.note: A serial number, or part of one.
One serial, with its latest event.
The asset (and any RMA) carrying this serial.
Every event for the serial, oldest first, with who recorded it.
The RMA returns list.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → All Assets → Serial Search.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-subnet
screenshots.alt: A subnet page with numbered callouts on Add IP, the address counts, the VLAN badge, the status filter and an address linked to an asset

annotate.note: Record an address in this subnet.
How many addresses are recorded, and how many are available, assigned or reserved.
The VLAN the subnet is on.
Show only available, assigned or reserved addresses.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr:has(a[href*='/assets/']) >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=4
annotate.note: The asset using the address. It opens the asset.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → IPAM → Subnets & IPs → a subnet.

screenshots.name: guide-assets-vlans
screenshots.alt: The VLAN list with numbered callouts on Add VLAN, a VLAN number and name, its colour, its subnet count and the view and edit buttons

annotate.note: Add a VLAN: number (1 to 4094), name, description and colour.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=1
annotate.note: The name opens the VLAN with the subnets on it.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=3
annotate.note: The colour used to tell VLANs apart.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=4
annotate.note: How many subnets are on the VLAN.
View or edit.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → IPAM → VLANs.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-rack-list
screenshots.alt: Infrastructure → Racks with numbered callouts on the Infrastructure tabs, Add Rack, a rack name, the type badge, the available units and the power bar

annotate.note: The Infrastructure tabs: Racks, Network Closets, Patch Panels and Port Configurations.
Add Rack. A customer must be selected first.
The rack name opens the rack page with its elevation.
Rack type. Network and data closets also appear under Network Closets.
Free units: the rack's size minus the units its placements take.
Allocated against capacity power, shown only when the rack has a power capacity.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Infrastructure → Racks.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-rack-detail
screenshots.alt: The rack page for HQ Comms Room — Rack A with numbered callouts on the header buttons, the info card, the tabs, the Front and Rear switch and the rack elevation drawn from catalog artwork

annotate.note: Add Asset to Rack places an asset (or a named item with no asset) at a start unit; Create New Asset makes the asset first.
Print a rack sheet.
Location, size, free units and, when set, power allocated against capacity.
Rack Visual, Mounted Assets (a table with edit and remove), Images and Wiring.
Show the front or the rear of the rack.
The elevation. A device with a catalog model is drawn from its artwork; anything else is a plain face with its saved name. Drag a device to another unit to move it; click it for details and Edit.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Infrastructure → Racks → a rack.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-rack-elevation
screenshots.alt: The hardware rack elevation for HQ Comms Room — Rack A with numbered callouts on the rack picker, Rack label, Rack settings, the front and rear export buttons and the placement table

annotate.note: Jump to another rack at this customer.
Rack label opens Labels with this rack selected.
Rack settings opens the rack page under Infrastructure, where placements are added and edited.
Export the front as SVG, PNG or PDF. The rear has its own buttons.
Every placement with its units, face, depth and hardware model. A name links to the hardware device when there is one.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Hardware & Ports → a rack.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-closet-detail
screenshots.alt: The network closet page for Floor 2 Network Closet with numbered callouts on the details card, the Rack View and Mounted Board switch, the asset sidebar, the mounted devices table, the visual layout and the patch panel port map

annotate.note: Type, building, floor, room, location, size and free units.
Rack View shows the unit elevation; Mounted Board is a free-form wall board where items are placed and resized anywhere.
This customer's assets. Drag one onto the unit grid to mount it.
Mounted Devices: every placement with its units, with edit and delete.
The same elevation as a rack, with a Front and Rear switch. Click a device to edit it and its ports.
Patch Panel Port Map: one grid for each placement whose name contains patch or panel. A port with a wiring connection is Patched; the rest are Empty.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Infrastructure → Network Closets → a closet.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-connectivity
screenshots.alt: Network Diagrams → Physical Connectivity for Client XYZ with numbered callouts on the site, search and category filters, the zoom buttons, Save layout, the export buttons, a device node and the legend

annotate.note: Limit the diagram to one site, or All sites.
Find a device by name or model: matches are highlighted, the rest dimmed, and the view moves to the first match.
Show one device category only (firewall, switch, patch panel and so on).
Save layout keeps the positions you dragged, for you.
Export SVG, PNG or PDF with the title, customer, legend and date.
A link is one or more documented cables; a red dashed mark is a path that continues but is not documented.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Network Diagrams → Physical Connectivity.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-vlan-view
screenshots.alt: Network Diagrams → VLAN View for Client XYZ with numbered callouts on the diagram tabs, the drawing and the legend for untagged, tagged and voice membership

annotate.note: The hardware pages: the two diagrams sit between VLAN Ports and Labels.
A device with ports in a VLAN is linked to that VLAN. The label counts its untagged, tagged and voice ports (U/T/V). Double-click a device to open it.
A solid line is native or untagged membership, a dashed one tagged or voice; U/T/V count the ports of each kind.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Network Diagrams → VLAN View.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-cable-list
screenshots.alt: Hardware & Ports → Cables for Client XYZ with numbered callouts on the search box, Export CSV, a cable ID, the A and B ends, and Print labels for selected cables

annotate.note: Search by cable ID, description or device.
Export this customer's cables as CSV.
The cable ID opens the cable to edit its type, colour, length, end labels and status.
The A and B ends: device and port, each linking to that port on the device page.
Tick cables, then print their labels.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Hardware & Ports → Cables.

screenshots.name: guide-infra-vlan-ports
screenshots.alt: Hardware & Ports → VLAN Ports for Client XYZ with numbered callouts on a VLAN chip, its group or scope, the untagged and tagged port counts, the VLAN diagram link and the Add VLAN and Add VLAN group forms

annotate.note: The VLAN number in its colour, the same colour the ports and diagrams use.
Client-wide, or the VLAN group (switching domain) it belongs to.
How many ports carry the VLAN untagged (native); the next column counts tagged ports.
VLAN diagram opens Network Diagrams → VLAN View.
Add a VLAN or a VLAN group. Shown only to people who can edit assets; saving also needs permission to create monitoring records.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Hardware & Ports → VLAN Ports.

screenshots.name: guide-stock-dashboard
screenshots.alt: The inventory dashboard with numbered callouts on the item count, the low stock count, the categories and locations counts, the recent transactions and the Add Item button

annotate.note: How many items this customer's inventory holds. Click to open All Items.
Items at or below their minimum quantity. Click to open Low Stock.
Categories. Locations, next to it, works the same way: click either to add, rename or remove them.
The last ten stock movements. View All opens the full transaction log.
Add an inventory item.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Inventory → Dashboard.

screenshots.name: guide-stock-items
screenshots.alt: The inventory item list with numbered callouts on the filters, Low Stock Only, an item name, a red low-stock quantity and the row buttons

annotate.note: Search by name, SKU or description, and filter by type and category.
Show only items at or below their minimum.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=0
annotate.note: The name opens the item, its QR code and its transaction history.
A red quantity means the item is at or below its minimum.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=7
annotate.note: View, Adjust Stock, Edit and Delete.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Inventory → All Items.

screenshots.name: guide-stock-item
screenshots.alt: An inventory item with numbered callouts on Adjust Stock, the quantity and minimum, and the transaction history

annotate.note: Adjust Stock: record stock coming in, going out or a correction.
Quantity on hand, the minimum that triggers Low Stock, the reorder quantity and the stock value.
Every recorded change: type, change, quantity after, reference (a PO or ticket), who and when.

screenshots.caption: An inventory item.

screenshots.name: guide-stock-tools
screenshots.alt: The tool list with numbered callouts on the search and Include retired switch, a tool code, where it is normally kept, its condition and Add tool

annotate.note: Search by name or code. Include retired also lists tools you have taken out of use.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=0
annotate.note: The tool's code, for example its asset tag.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr >> nth=0 >> td >> nth=3
annotate.note: Normally kept: the van it rides in, or else its storage location.

annotate.selector: main tbody tr:has-text('Needs service') >> td >> nth=4
annotate.note: Condition: good, needs service, out of service or lost.
Add a tool.

screenshots.caption: Assets & Network → Inventory → Tools.

screenshots.name: guide-stock-vehicle
